001package io.jstach.rainbowgum.scopedkeyvalues;
002
003import java.util.Map;
004import java.util.ServiceLoader;
005import java.util.function.BiConsumer;
006
007import io.jstach.rainbowgum.scopedkeyvalues.spi.ScopedKeyValuesProvider;
008import io.jstach.rainbowgum.scopedkeyvalues.spi.ScopedKeyValuesProviderFactory;
009
010/**
011 * Request/task-scoped key values, pushed once (typically once, wrapping an entire request
012 * or task at its boundary) and never mutated afterward.
013 * <p>
014 * This is deliberately not a replacement for ad-hoc, imperative, single-call-site key
015 * values (e.g. SLF4J's own {@code LoggingEventBuilder#addKeyValue(String, Object)}) -
016 * that is still the right tool for "add this to just this one log line". This class is
017 * for the opposite shape: a small number of values that should be visible on every log
018 * line for an entire request/task, set up once, at a well-known boundary.
019 * <p>
020 * The actual push/read mechanism is supplied by whichever {@link ScopedKeyValuesProvider}
021 * is found via {@link ServiceLoader} the first time this class is used - the same
022 * bootstrap shape SLF4J itself uses for {@code org.slf4j.spi.SLF4JServiceProvider}. If
023 * none is found, pushing still runs the body normally, it just does not record or
024 * propagate anything - always safe to depend on this module alone, even with nothing
025 * bound.
026 */
027public final class ScopedKeyValues {
028
029        /*
030         * A plain static final field is the only option on this project's current JDK
031         * baseline, computed eagerly at class-init time via the usual "safe publication
032         * through a final field" guarantee. If/when this project's baseline reaches a JDK
033         * with JEP 502 (Stable Values), this is a candidate to become a StableValue<...>
034         * instead - same one-time, thread-safe, at-most-once computation, but computed lazily
035         * on first access rather than tied to class initialization, without needing a
036         * holder-class trick to get that laziness.
037         */
038        private static final ScopedKeyValuesProvider PROVIDER = findProvider();
039
040        private ScopedKeyValues() {
041        }
042
043        private static ScopedKeyValuesProvider findProvider() {
044                for (var factory : ServiceLoader.load(ScopedKeyValuesProviderFactory.class)) {
045                        return factory.provide();
046                }
047                return NoopScopedKeyValuesProvider.INSTANCE;
048        }
049
050        /**
051         * Every currently pushed layer, merged into one map - later (more-deeply-nested)
052         * pushes win on a key collision.
053         * @return merged, read-only-by-convention map, empty if nothing is currently pushed
054         * or no {@link ScopedKeyValuesProvider} was found.
055         */
056        public static Map<String, String> currentMerged() {
057                return PROVIDER.currentMerged();
058        }
059
060        /**
061         * Creates a builder to push a new layer of key values, fetched fresh from whichever
062         * {@link ScopedKeyValuesProvider} is active.
063         * @return builder.
064         */
065        public static Builder builder() {
066                return PROVIDER.builder();
067        }
068
069        /**
070         * Like {@code java.lang.ScopedValue.CallableOp} but declared here so this API module
071         * never has to reference {@code java.lang.ScopedValue} itself, keeping it compilable
072         * on older JDKs - the real {@code ScopedValue}-backed provider (a separate module
073         * requiring a newer JDK) bridges the two with a plain method reference, since both
074         * interfaces share the same {@code R call() throws X} shape.
075         *
076         * @param <R> return type.
077         * @param <X> exception type the operation may throw.
078         */
079        @FunctionalInterface
080        public interface CallableOp<R, X extends Throwable> {
081
082                /**
083                 * Runs the operation.
084                 * @return result.
085                 * @throws X whatever the operation itself declares.
086                 */
087                R call() throws X;
088
089        }
090
091        /**
092         * Builds one immutable layer of key values and pushes it for the duration of a
093         * {@link #run(Runnable)}/{@link #call(CallableOp)} call. Implemented by whichever
094         * {@link ScopedKeyValuesProvider} is active, so an addition can be written directly
095         * into that provider's own internal representation instead of always collecting into
096         * an intermediate {@link Map} first.
097         * <p>
098         * Extends {@link BiConsumer} (rather than only offering a bespoke
099         * {@code add(String, String)} method) so a builder can be populated directly from any
100         * existing {@code BiConsumer}-shaped source of key values, the same idiom
101         * {@code io.jstach.rainbowgum.KeyValues#forEach(BiConsumer)} already uses.
102         */
103        public interface Builder extends BiConsumer<String, String> {
104
105                /**
106                 * Fluent form of {@link #accept(Object, Object)}.
107                 * @param key key, never {@code null}.
108                 * @param value value, never {@code null} - pass a real sentinel/empty string
109                 * instead if "no value" needs to be represented, rather than relying on null
110                 * analysis to catch a missing one.
111                 * @return this.
112                 * @throws NullPointerException if either argument is {@code null}.
113                 */
114                default Builder add(String key, String value) {
115                        accept(key, value);
116                        return this;
117                }
118
119                /**
120                 * Pushes this layer and runs {@code body} for its duration.
121                 * @param body code to run with this layer pushed.
122                 */
123                void run(Runnable body);
124
125                /**
126                 * Pushes this layer and calls {@code body} for its duration.
127                 * @param <T> return type.
128                 * @param <X> exception type {@code body} may throw.
129                 * @param body code to call with this layer pushed.
130                 * @return whatever {@code body} returns.
131                 * @throws X whatever {@code body} throws.
132                 */
133                <T, X extends Throwable> T call(CallableOp<T, X> body) throws X;
134
135        }
136
137}
